name: Heart
overview: A four-chambered muscular organ located in the middle mediastinum, with its apex directed inferiorly and to the left.
relations: The fibrous pericardium surrounds the heart; the great vessels enter and leave its base.
function: The right heart directs systemic venous blood to pulmonary circulation, while the left heart pumps oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation.
clinical: Coronary artery obstruction may cause myocardial ischemia or infarction.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Aorta
overview: The main systemic artery arising from the left ventricle.
relations: The ascending aorta continues into the arch and descending thoracic and abdominal aorta.
function: Distributes oxygenated blood to systemic tissues.
clinical: Aortic aneurysm and dissection may cause life-threatening hemorrhage.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Lungs
overview: Paired organs of gas exchange surrounded by visceral pleura. The right lung typically has three lobes and the left two.
relations: The pulmonary hila contain bronchi, pulmonary arteries and veins, bronchial vessels, lymphatics, and nerves.
function: Gas exchange occurs across the alveolar–capillary barrier.
clinical: Pulmonary embolism, pneumothorax and pneumonia can compromise ventilation or perfusion.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Diaphragm
overview: A dome-shaped musculotendinous partition between the thorax and abdomen.
relations: The central tendon is attached to the muscular periphery; the inferior vena cava, esophagus and aorta traverse separate openings.
function: Primary muscle of quiet inspiration.
clinical: Phrenic nerve injury can cause hemidiaphragm weakness.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Brain
overview: The principal integrative organ of the central nervous system, comprising cerebrum, diencephalon, brainstem and cerebellum.
relations: Surrounded by meninges and cerebrospinal fluid; supplied predominantly by internal carotid and vertebrobasilar arterial systems.
function: Integrates sensory information, movement, cognition, autonomic control and homeostasis.
clinical: Stroke may present with deficits dependent on the involved vascular territory.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Cerebellum
overview: A posterior fossa structure with hemispheres and a vermis.
relations: Posterior to the brainstem and inferior to the occipital lobes, separated by the tentorium cerebelli.
function: Coordinates movement, posture and motor learning.
clinical: Lesions may cause ataxia, dysmetria and intention tremor.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Spinal cord
overview: Part of the central nervous system continuing from the medulla oblongata.
relations: Protected by vertebrae and meninges; adult spinal cord usually terminates near L1–L2 vertebral level.
function: Conducts ascending sensory and descending motor pathways and mediates spinal reflexes.
clinical: Cord compression can produce weakness, sensory changes and autonomic dysfunction.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Liver
overview: A large glandular organ beneath the right hemidiaphragm.
relations: Related to the gallbladder, stomach, duodenum, right kidney and diaphragm.
function: Processes nutrients, synthesizes plasma proteins, metabolizes toxins and produces bile.
clinical: Portal hypertension can cause ascites and portosystemic collateral formation.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Stomach
overview: A distensible muscular digestive organ between the esophagus and duodenum.
relations: Lies primarily in the left upper abdomen; its greater curvature is related to the greater omentum.
function: Stores food, mechanically mixes it and begins protein digestion via acid and pepsin.
clinical: Peptic ulcers may cause upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Small intestine
overview: The duodenum, jejunum and ileum form the major site for nutrient absorption.
relations: Mesenteric attachments suspend the jejunum and ileum; the duodenum is mostly retroperitoneal.
function: Digestion and absorption of nutrients and water.
clinical: Mesenteric ischemia can cause severe abdominal pain.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Kidneys
overview: Paired retroperitoneal organs containing nephrons, cortex, medulla, calyces and renal pelvis.
relations: The renal hila transmit renal vessels, nerves, lymphatics and the ureter.
function: Filter plasma, regulate fluid and electrolyte balance, and contribute to endocrine homeostasis.
clinical: Renal obstruction or ischemia can reduce kidney function.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Urinary bladder
overview: A muscular reservoir for urine, located behind the pubic symphysis.
relations: The ureters enter posteriorly; the urethra exits inferiorly through the bladder neck.
function: Stores urine and expels it during micturition.
clinical: Neurogenic bladder may lead to retention or incontinence.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Femur
overview: The longest and strongest bone of the human skeleton.
relations: Proximally forms the hip joint; distally articulates with tibia and patella at the knee.
function: Provides weight-bearing support and lever arms for locomotion.
clinical: Femoral neck fractures may disrupt retinacular vessels and predispose to avascular necrosis.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Humerus
overview: The long bone of the arm extending from shoulder to elbow.
relations: The radial nerve travels in the radial groove of the posterior shaft.
function: Provides attachment for upper-limb muscles and contributes to shoulder and elbow motion.
clinical: Midshaft fractures can injure the radial nerve.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Scapula
overview: A flat triangular bone with glenoid cavity, spine, acromion and coracoid process.
relations: Moves over the thoracic wall and articulates with clavicle at the acromioclavicular joint.
function: Provides muscle attachment and positions the glenoid for upper limb movement.
clinical: Scapular winging may follow long thoracic nerve injury.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Biceps brachii
overview: A two-headed muscle of the anterior compartment of the arm.
relations: The long head arises from the supraglenoid tubercle and short head from the coracoid process.
function: Flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; assists shoulder flexion.
clinical: Long-head tendinopathy may present with anterior shoulder pain.

fields.Origin: Supraglenoid tubercle (long head); coracoid process (short head)

reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Deltoid
overview: A thick triangular muscle covering the glenohumeral joint.
relations: Arises from lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine.
function: Middle fibers abduct the arm; anterior and posterior fibers contribute to flexion/medial rotation and extension/lateral rotation.
clinical: Axillary nerve injury can weaken shoulder abduction.

fields.Origin: Lateral third of clavicle, acromion, spine of scapula

reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Trapezius
overview: A broad superficial muscle of the posterior neck and upper back.
relations: Spans occiput, nuchal ligament and spinous processes to the clavicle and scapular spine.
function: Elevates, retracts, depresses and upwardly rotates the scapula.
clinical: Spinal accessory nerve dysfunction may cause shoulder droop.

fields.Innervation: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with cervical sensory/proprioceptive contributions

reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Gluteus maximus
overview: A large superficial muscle of the gluteal region.
relations: Extends from ilium, sacrum and coccyx to the iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity.
function: Extends and laterally rotates the hip, especially during rising and climbing.
clinical: Inferior gluteal nerve injury weakens hip extension.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Rectus femoris
overview: The only quadriceps head that crosses both the hip and knee.
relations: Arises from anterior inferior iliac spine and superior acetabular region.
function: Extends the knee and assists hip flexion.
clinical: Strain can occur with forceful kicking or sprinting.

fields.Insertion: Patella via quadriceps tendon, tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament

reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Gastrocnemius
overview: A superficial two-headed muscle of the posterior leg.
relations: Originates near the medial and lateral femoral condyles and joins the calcaneal tendon.
function: Plantarflexes the ankle and assists knee flexion.
clinical: Injury may present as an acute calf strain.
reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Sternocleidomastoid
overview: A paired superficial cervical muscle extending from sternum and clavicle to the mastoid process.
relations: Divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.
function: Unilaterally rotates the face contralaterally and laterally flexes the neck; bilaterally flexes the neck.
clinical: Congenital muscular torticollis may affect head position.

fields.Innervation: Spinal accessory nerve (motor); C2–C3 sensory/proprioceptive contributions

reference: MedStudy authored reference cards; confirm with standard anatomy references before public medical teaching.

name: Skin
overview: The outer covering of the body, composed of epidermis, dermis, and underlying associated structures.
function: Acts as a protective barrier, contributes to sensation and thermoregulation.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Epidermis
overview: The superficial epithelial component of skin, composed primarily of keratinocytes.
function: Forms a water-resistant barrier and participates in cutaneous defense.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Dermis
overview: The connective-tissue layer beneath the epidermis containing vessels, nerves, follicles, and glands.
function: Provides strength, elasticity, nutrition to the epidermis, and sensory support.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Hair follicles
overview: Epidermal appendages extending into the dermis from which hair shafts grow.
function: Produce hair and contribute to cutaneous sensation.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Sebaceous glands
overview: Holocrine glands usually connected to hair follicles within the dermis.
function: Release sebum that contributes to lubrication of skin and hair.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Pituitary gland
overview: An endocrine organ in the hypophyseal fossa of the sphenoid bone connected to the hypothalamus.
function: Releases hormones involved in growth, metabolism, reproduction, and water balance.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Thyroid gland
overview: An anterior cervical endocrine gland situated around the upper trachea, usually comprising two lobes and an isthmus.
function: Produces thyroid hormones and calcitonin.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Parathyroid glands
overview: Small endocrine glands commonly located on the posterior aspect of the thyroid gland.
function: Secrete parathyroid hormone involved in calcium homeostasis.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Adrenal glands
overview: Paired endocrine organs located superomedially to the kidneys, each with cortex and medulla.
function: Produce steroid hormones and catecholamines.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Pancreatic islets
overview: Endocrine cell clusters distributed throughout the pancreas.
function: Secrete hormones including insulin and glucagon to regulate metabolism.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Spleen
overview: A lymphoid organ in the left upper abdomen, related to the stomach and diaphragm.
function: Filters blood and participates in immune surveillance.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Thymus
overview: A primary lymphoid organ situated in the anterior mediastinum, most prominent in childhood.
function: Supports T lymphocyte maturation.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Lymph nodes
overview: Small encapsulated lymphoid structures distributed along lymphatic vessels.
function: Filter lymph and support antigen-driven immune responses.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Thoracic duct
overview: A major lymphatic channel ascending through the thorax to drain near the left venous angle.
function: Returns lymph from much of the body to the venous circulation.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Uterus
overview: A hollow muscular pelvic organ between the urinary bladder and rectum, comprising fundus, body, and cervix.
function: Supports implantation, gestation, and parturition.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Ovaries
overview: Paired female gonads located in the pelvis adjacent to the uterus.
function: Produce oocytes and secrete ovarian hormones.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Uterine tubes
overview: Paired muscular tubes extending from the uterine cornua toward the ovaries.
function: Transport oocytes and commonly provide the site of fertilization.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Testes
overview: Paired male gonads within the scrotum, composed of seminiferous tubules and interstitial tissue.
function: Produce spermatozoa and testosterone.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Prostate gland
overview: An accessory male reproductive gland located inferior to the urinary bladder and surrounding the prostatic urethra.
function: Contributes secretions to seminal fluid.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Superior vena cava
overview: A large systemic vein returning blood from structures superior to the diaphragm to the right atrium.
function: Conducts deoxygenated systemic venous blood to the heart.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Inferior vena cava
overview: A major vein ascending on the right side of the aorta and entering the right atrium.
function: Returns systemic venous blood from the lower body to the heart.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Pulmonary trunk
overview: A major artery arising from the right ventricle and dividing into right and left pulmonary arteries.
function: Carries blood toward the lungs for gas exchange.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Trachea
overview: An air-conducting tube with C-shaped cartilage rings extending from the larynx to the main bronchi.
function: Conducts and conditions inspired air.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Bronchial tree
overview: The branching airways formed by the main, lobar, segmental, and smaller bronchi.
function: Distributes air through the pulmonary parenchyma.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Urethra
overview: A duct carrying urine from the bladder to the exterior, with sex-specific anatomical course and relationships.
function: Provides the distal pathway for urinary elimination.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Large intestine
overview: The distal gastrointestinal tract containing cecum, colon, rectum, and anal canal.
function: Absorbs water and electrolytes and stores and conveys fecal material.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Gallbladder
overview: A pear-shaped sac on the visceral surface of the liver communicating with the biliary tree.
function: Stores and concentrates bile between meals.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Spinal nerves
overview: Paired mixed nerves formed by union of anterior and posterior roots of spinal cord segments.
function: Convey somatic and autonomic sensory and motor fibers.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Pelvis
overview: The bony ring of paired hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx forming the basin between trunk and lower limbs.
function: Transfers trunk loads to lower limbs and protects pelvic organs.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Mandible
overview: The lower jaw bone forming joints with the temporal bones.
function: Supports lower dentition and jaw movements.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Ribs
overview: Curved bones articulating posteriorly with thoracic vertebrae and contributing to the thoracic cage.
function: Protect thoracic organs and support respiratory movement.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Clavicle
overview: An S-shaped long bone connecting the sternum to the scapula at the acromioclavicular joint.
function: Acts as a strut supporting the shoulder girdle.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Pectoralis major
overview: A large superficial anterior chest muscle attaching to the humerus.
function: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; portions also assist arm flexion.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Latissimus dorsi
overview: A broad back muscle extending from trunk structures to the proximal humerus.
function: Extends, adducts, and medially rotates the upper limb.
reference: MedStudy original editorial summary; verify against primary anatomical references before use in formal teaching.

name: Left atrium
overview: A posterior heart chamber receiving oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins.
function: Transfers blood through the mitral valve to the left ventricle.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Right atrium
overview: A right-sided heart chamber receiving systemic venous blood through the venae cavae and coronary sinus.
function: Transfers blood through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Left ventricle
overview: A thick-walled cardiac chamber communicating with the left atrium and aorta.
function: Ejects oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Right ventricle
overview: An anterior cardiac chamber communicating with the right atrium and pulmonary trunk.
function: Ejects blood into the pulmonary circulation.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Mitral valve
overview: A two-leaflet atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and left ventricle.
function: Helps prevent backward flow during ventricular systole.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Tricuspid valve
overview: The atrioventricular valve separating right atrium and right ventricle.
function: Helps prevent backward flow during ventricular systole.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Aortic valve
overview: A semilunar valve between the left ventricle and ascending aorta.
function: Prevents backward flow from the aorta into the left ventricle during diastole.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Pulmonary valve
overview: A semilunar valve between the right ventricle and pulmonary trunk.
function: Prevents backward flow into the right ventricle during diastole.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Esophagus
overview: A muscular tube passing from the pharynx through the thorax to the stomach.
function: Transports swallowed material via coordinated peristalsis.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Duodenum
overview: The first portion of the small intestine receiving gastric contents, bile, and pancreatic secretions.
function: Neutralizes chyme and participates in digestion and absorption.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Jejunum
overview: The middle portion of the small intestine between duodenum and ileum.
function: A major site of nutrient absorption.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Ileum
overview: The terminal part of the small intestine joining the cecum at the ileocecal junction.
function: Absorbs nutrients including vitamin B12 and bile salts.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Pancreas
overview: A retroperitoneal gland behind the stomach consisting of head, body and tail.
function: Provides digestive enzymes and endocrine hormones.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Cecum
overview: A pouch-like initial part of the large intestine adjacent to the ileocecal junction.
function: Receives ileal contents and begins colonic processing.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Ascending colon
overview: The colonic segment ascending from cecum toward hepatic flexure.
function: Absorbs water and transports intestinal contents.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Descending colon
overview: The colonic segment extending from splenic flexure into the sigmoid colon.
function: Conveys and stores intestinal contents.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Rectum
overview: A terminal pelvic segment of the large intestine continuous with sigmoid colon and anal canal.
function: Stores feces before defecation.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Larynx
overview: A cartilaginous airway structure between pharynx and trachea containing the vocal folds.
function: Participates in phonation and protection of the lower airway.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Right lung
overview: The right pulmonary organ, commonly divided into superior, middle and inferior lobes.
function: Participates in gas exchange across its alveoli.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Left lung
overview: The left pulmonary organ, typically with superior and inferior lobes and a cardiac notch.
function: Participates in gas exchange across its alveoli.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Alveoli
overview: Microscopic air spaces in the distal pulmonary parenchyma enclosed by thin walls.
function: Provide surface for exchange of respiratory gases.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Right kidney
overview: The right paired retroperitoneal kidney beneath the liver.
function: Filters blood, regulates fluid balance and produces urine.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Left kidney
overview: The left paired retroperitoneal kidney.
function: Filters blood, regulates fluid balance and produces urine.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Ureter
overview: A muscular duct conveying urine from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder.
function: Transports urine by peristaltic contractions.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Renal cortex
overview: The peripheral zone of kidney containing renal corpuscles and sections of nephrons.
function: Participates in filtration and tubular handling.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Renal medulla
overview: The inner kidney containing medullary pyramids and loops of Henle.
function: Supports urine concentration and transport.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Cerebrum
overview: The largest part of the brain with cerebral hemispheres and cortical and subcortical regions.
function: Supports perception, voluntary movement, cognition and language.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Brainstem
overview: The neural axis consisting of midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.
function: Contains ascending and descending pathways and major autonomic nuclei.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Medulla oblongata
overview: The caudal part of the brainstem continuous with the spinal cord.
function: Contains multiple vital autonomic and sensory-motor nuclei.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Hippocampus
overview: A medial temporal-lobe structure forming part of the hippocampal formation.
function: Important for memory formation.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Corpus callosum
overview: A large commissural white-matter tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres.
function: Supports interhemispheric communication.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Optic nerve
overview: The second cranial nerve formed by retinal ganglion cell axons.
function: Transmits visual information toward the brain.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Femoral artery
overview: A major arterial vessel of the lower limb passing through the femoral triangle.
function: Supplies the thigh and provides distal lower-limb arterial flow.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Carotid artery
overview: A major paired arterial conduit in the neck supplying the head and neck.
function: Provides arterial blood to head and neck regions.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Brachial plexus
overview: A network of nerve roots and trunks in the neck and axillary region.
function: Provides much of the peripheral innervation of the upper limb.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Tendon
overview: Dense regular connective tissue commonly connecting muscle to bone.
function: Transmits forces generated by muscle contraction.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Ligament
overview: A fibrous connective tissue structure connecting bones and supporting joints.
function: Contributes to joint stability.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Sternum
overview: A flat anterior thoracic bone comprising manubrium, body and xiphoid process.
function: Provides an anterior attachment for ribs and protects mediastinal structures.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Sacrum
overview: A triangular bone formed by fused sacral vertebrae at the posterior pelvis.
function: Transfers trunk weight to the pelvis.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Radius
overview: The lateral forearm bone in anatomical position.
function: Participates in elbow, forearm and wrist articulations.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Ulna
overview: The medial forearm bone in anatomical position.
function: Provides the major stabilizing articulation of the elbow.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Tibia
overview: The medial, weight-bearing long bone of the leg.
function: Transmits load from femur to ankle.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Fibula
overview: The lateral bone of the leg, relatively less weight-bearing than the tibia.
function: Supports ankle stability and provides muscle attachment sites.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Quadriceps femoris
overview: A group of four muscles on the anterior thigh.
function: Primarily extends the knee.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Biceps femoris
overview: A posterior thigh muscle in the hamstring group.
function: Flexes knee and contributes to hip extension via its long head.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Soleus
overview: A broad posterior leg muscle deep to gastrocnemius.
function: Plantarflexes the foot, especially during standing.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.

name: Rotator cuff
overview: A group of four shoulder muscles and tendons associated with the glenohumeral joint.
function: Stabilizes the humeral head and assists shoulder movement.
reference: MedStudy original educational summary; independent medical review required.
